I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked for me last year, then I adjust a little for price, water, and what I see around me in Quzhou. Here, wheat-maize is still the main road for steady grain, and with my well I do not want to leave land dry when water is needed. I have 16.9 mu total, so I will keep most of the land in wheat followed by maize, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Cotton can still make money, but it takes more watching and more picking, and with some people in my family working outside, I do not want too much cotton area. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, and improved cotton seed, because now most people around me use those and the stand is better. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the crop go hungry, especially for wheat and maize. Wheat I will feed heavier because I want strong tillers and good heads. Maize I will also feed well because if rain and irrigation match, maize answers fertilizer fast. Cotton I will not push too hard with nitrogen or it grows too much stalk and not enough bolls. For irrigation, wheat will get the most attention, maize a couple times if summer rain is short, and cotton a few times at key stages. On pesticide, wheat is usually lighter, maize watches worms and leaf disease, and cotton needs more sprays because insects can come one after another. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage on most ground because it is quicker and costs less than deep ploughing every year, and it works with my scale.
